memory_update.text: AMKR should remain the U.S.-listed reference anchor for memory/backend OSAT overflow because it is directly in outsourced semiconductor packaging and test, including memory and wafer-level processing.
FORM is a high-priority underfollowed discovery candidate for AI memory bottlenecks because probe cards sit in the qualification/yield layer for DRAM, HBM, and NAND.

COHU is a focused small-cap discovery candidate for HBM inspection and handler capacity, but materiality must be tested because disclosed HBM revenue is still modest relative to total company revenue.

Need a follow-up pass on non-US-listed pure-play memory OSATs and Asian test houses, especially Powertech and other Taiwan/Korea/Japan backend suppliers, because they may be closer to the actual DDR/NAND overflow than US-listed names.

The key falsification test for this node is whether memory/backend overflow produces measurable utilization, pricing, order, or margin improvement at third-party OSAT/test suppliers rather than being fully absorbed by in-house memory producers.

node: Memory backend, OSAT, DRAM/NAND packaging and testing overflow
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the hypothesis that AI/HBM demand crowds out memory backend capacity and pushes conventional DRAM, NAND, packaging, inspection, probe, handler, and burn-in work toward qualified third-party OSAT and semiconductor test-equipment suppliers. The strongest US-listed direct anchor is Amkor as a U.S.-headquartered OSAT. The more underfollowed discovery names are FormFactor, Cohu, and Kulicke & Soffa, which sit in probe cards, HBM/DRAM inspection or handling, and advanced memory packaging equipment rather than obvious GPU or HBM producer categories. Claims are research leads only, not investment recommendations.
